d:
I think you should know that it wasn't actually the Gnolls who attacked us on the road.
We were actually attacked by a giant, wolf-like creature that I now know as a "worgen". It dispatched our guards and came for me, but Banon threw himself in its path. I managed to get a spell off which startled the creature, causing it to flee, but Banon was already badly bitten. He insisted I leave him there but I refused.
We were limping back here when the gnolls found us. What came next was terrifying...
c:
So now you understand. At the very end of his strength after being pierced by a dozen gnoll blades, he reared up to strike me. In that final moment we locked eyes, and I could tell he still knew who he was and that he recognized me. He knew what was happening but he had no control over himself. That was the worst part.
If such a thing is possible, I will see the creature that doomed him dead so that it can never visit this horror on another living thing. I swear it upon the sky above.

d:
Trevan tells me that the worgen are a major threat to the citizens of Silverpine Forest. Despite their strength and resilience they can be killed, but there is one in particular that just doesn't ever seem to stay dead due to unknown magic.
That's the one that attacked us. He is known as Old Fire-Eye and he is the biggest and meanest of their kind. To put him down, we'll need a special kind of weapon.
Speak with Trevan and he will supply you with a list of what is needed to forge such a weapon.
p: Trust in the light to guide your blade. However, the light needs a good blade to guide.
c: Now that we've got the materials we need, we just need a smith to craft the blade for us. I think I know just such a smith.

d:
Before we fled Gnomeregan, I made a hard copy of my family's archives. Arcanotechnical field equations, Second War submarine hull designs, Grandma Quikswitch's chili recipe... Our greatest accomplishments are in those files.
It wasn't until we reached Ironforge that I found a hole in my pack! Several punch cards are gone, and without them the data's too scrambled to recover.
The cards must be buried in the snow, somewhere outside Gnomeregan. Could you find them? I know it's a long shot...
p: How is the data retrieval progressing?
c: These cards seem a bit damp... But I can work with this! Thank you, friend!

d:
A Forsaken adventurer... Here in Ashenvale? Amusing.
So you seek a Kor Gem? Unsurprising as these are sometimes employed to empower magical weapons and implements by the adventurers of the Alliance. Why should a fallen adventurer like you be any different?
If you truly desire one of the gems, then you must head north to the ruins known as Blackfathom Deeps. The naga who still use the gems are down below. Do not go alone, adventurer.
p: Kor gems can be used for great acts of evil. Far be it from me to judge if your intentions are pure. It matters not to me.
c:
You'll no doubt notice the corruption that permeates this gem. For your purposes, the magic needed to dispel the evil that the naga witches have infused into the gem is rather simple. A shame really, there's much one could learn from such powers.
I don't suppose you'd be willing to abandon whatever quest caused you to seek this gem, and sell it to me instead? It could prove valuable to my... Academic pursuits.

d:
What a view... Best an old man can ask for.
The fish sure are bitin' now, though I'm down to my last bait. I don't suppose you have any spare fishing supplies on you? Of course not, forgive me. I get so excited at the thought of casting another line it didn't dawn on me I may be one of the few carrying supplies everywhere I go.
Would you be able to help refresh my stock? Catherine Leland has an assortment of fishing goods just west of the Trade District along the canals. Tell her old Gray sent you.
p: Did you get the fishing supplies?
c:
Great timing! Caught a big one with my last bait. Great day so far. They're really biting out here!
Tell you what, since you were kind enough to keep this old man in business how about a few fish for the road?
